R298.note: Captures next before free in both branches; traversal order, single free, and refresh_session calls are unchanged.

R299.note: Key-to-path allowlist keeps the caller string off File.ReadAllText as the contract requires; the three hardcoded keys/paths are placeholders the write-up shows but does not label as needing real values.

R300.note: filterArgs overload lets the JNDI provider escape RFC 2254 metacharacters; passing null SearchControls matches the original.

R301.note: Dropping template.HTML restores html/template contextual escaping; nothing else in the handler changes.

R302.note: CGI::escapeHTML at the output sink; encoding ticket_id and priority is a stated no-op for their constrained values.

R303.note: resolve(strict=True) plus is_relative_to containment, same 404 paths; only unstated dependency is Python 3.9+ for is_relative_to.

R304.note: Named-parameter binding closes the injection, but the backslash LIKE escaping is added without an HQL escape clause - HQL has no default escape, so on SQL Server/Oracle a term containing _ or % is sent as a literal backslash sequence and fails to match products it matched before, contrary to the write-up's claim.

R305.note: Gate::authorize enforces the same policy check and yields a 403 on denial; no other change.

R306.note: validate_csrf blocks forged POSTs before the write, but it raises wtforms ValidationError rather than CSRFError, so the except clause never fires and a missing/invalid token produces a 500 instead of the stated 400; template must also be updated to emit the token (stated).

R307.note: SqlParameter binding replaces concatenation; the stated NVarChar(256) size would only silently truncate an owner value longer than 256 characters.

R308.note: Extension allowlist plus libmagic sniff closes the dangerous-type upload, but the sniff rejects legitimate files libmagic labels differently (docx reported as application/zip on older libmagic, .txt content reported as text/csv, text/html, etc.) and adds a native libmagic dependency.

R309.note: Verb-to-handler map is the right shape for a callable-string dispatch, but the write-up fabricates three handler functions with invented replies and changes the argument convention from spread positional args to a single array, so any real handler set is silently replaced.

R310.note: jwt.verify with a pinned algorithm list and a key from JWT_SECRET; the new startup requirement for that env var is stated plainly and is intrinsic to verifying a signature.

R311.note: realpath on both sides plus path.relative containment, reading the checked realTarget; nonexistent paths still return the original 404.

R312.note: path.relative containment after join blocks .. escapes and cross-drive absolutes; the new 400 for rejected names is stated, and only a filename literally beginning with '..' is over-rejected.
